text: The distance between Sun and Earth is R. The duration of year if the distance between Sun and Earth becomes 3R will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

$T^{2}$ $\propto$ $R^{3}$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{T^{'}}{T}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{3R}{R}\right )^{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{T^{'}}{T}=3\sqrt{3}$

$\Rightarrow T^{'}=3\sqrt{3}$ years

text: A proton, a deuteron and an $α$-particle with same kinetic energy enter into a uniform magnetic field at right angle to magnetic field. The ratio of the radii of their respective circular paths is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a charge moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, $qvB=\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$, so

$r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$

With the same $K$ and $B$, $r\propto \dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{q}$. The proton has mass $m$ and charge $e$, the deuteron $2m$ and $e$, and the $α$-particle $4m$ and $2e$:

$r_{p}:r_{d}:r_{α}=\dfrac{\sqrt{1}}{1}:\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{1}:\dfrac{\sqrt{4}}{2}=1:\sqrt{2}:1$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: An electric bulb is rated as 200 W. What will be the peak magnetic field at 4 m distance produced by the radiations coming from this bulb? Consider this bulb as a point source with 3.5% efficiency.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The total power $(P_{T})$ of the light bulb is given as 200 W, but only 3.5% of this power is actually emitted as radiation, which we will call P. 

So, Effective power output of the bulb

$\mathrm{P}=\frac{3\cdot 5}{100}\times 200=7\mathrm{W}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{Intensity}\mathrm{I} & =\dfrac{\mathrm{P}}{4πr^{2}}=\dfrac{7}{4π(4)^{2}}\mathrm{W}/\mathrm{m}^{2} \\  \\ \text{Intensity}\mathrm{I} & =\text{Average energy density}\times c \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\in _{0}\mathrm{E}_{0}^{2}c \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\mathrm{B}_{0}^{2}}{μ_{0}}c \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \mathrm{B}_{0} & =\sqrt{\dfrac{2μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{c}} \\  \\ =\sqrt{\dfrac{2\times 4π\times 10^{-7}\times 7}{3\times 10^{8}\times 4π\times 16}} \\  \\ =1.71\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{T} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: A body is projected from the ground at an angle of 45${}^{\circ }$ with the horizontal. Its velocity after 2s is $20 ms^{-1}$. The maximum height reached by the body during its motion is $__________ m. ($use $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $u$ be the speed of projection. The horizontal velocity stays $u\cos 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$, and the vertical velocity at $t=2\text{s}$ is $\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}-gt=\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}-20$.

The speed at $t=2\text{s}$ is $20\text{m s}^{-1}$. Writing $a=\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$:

$a^{2}+(a-20)^{2}=20^{2}\Rightarrow 2a^{2}-40a=0\Rightarrow a=20\text{m s}^{-1}$

($a=0$ would mean no projection.) So $u\sin 45^{\circ }=20\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $u=20\sqrt{2}\text{m s}^{-1}$; at $t=2\text{s}$ the vertical velocity is zero, so the body is at its highest point moving horizontally at $20\text{m s}^{-1}$.

$H=\frac{(u\sin 45^{\circ })^{2}}{2g}=\frac{20^{2}}{2\times 10}=20\text{m}$

Hence, the answer is 20.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: A monoatomic gas performs a work of $\frac{Q}{4}$ where Q is the heat supplied to it. The molar heat capacity of the gas will be $______________ R$ during this transformation. Where R is the gas constant.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By $1^{st}$ law,

$\Delta U=\Delta Q-\frac{\Delta Q}{4}=\frac{3}{4}\Delta Q$

$\Rightarrow nC_{v}\Delta T=\frac{3}{4}nC\Delta T$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{4C_{v}}{3}=2R$
